Objective: To investigate structure of muscle and cytoskeleton
proteins titin and nebulin in stiff person syndrome (SPS).
Background: A 49-year-old lady with stiffness and tension of
axial muscles developed vertical diplopia, dysarthrophonia, ataxia.
Brain MRI was normal. Global electromyography (EMG) showed
increased bioelectrical activity in axial muscles. Increase of anti-
bodies against glutamic acid decarboxylase was found. SPS was
diagnosed.
Design and methods:Biopsy from erector spinae muscle was ana-
lyzed using morphological and immuno-histochemical techniques;
titin, nebulin were investigated by gel-electrophoresis.
Results: Structure of the muscle tissue was normal. Analysis of
myosin heavy chains showed predominance of type I fibres. We
were first to investigate titin and nebulin in SPS: twofold decrease
was found.
Conclusions: Sustained increase of muscle activity leads to
destruction of titin and nebulin that result in impairment of sup-
porting/elastic properties of muscle sarcomere cytoskeleton, and to
reorganization of muscle tissue with slow fatigue resistant fibres
predominance.
